• Retail shops (fashion, home goods, gifts)
• Restaurants and bars
• Art installations and pop‑up events | | **Accessibility** | Close to the 14th St/8th St subway station (A, C, E, L lines) and within walking distance of many Midtown attractions. | | **Visitor mix** | Tourists, locals, food‑bloggers, and families. | | **Special events** | Seasonal festivals, cooking classes, and live music. | ### How it compares to other NYC markets | Market | Approx. annual visitors | Notes | |--------|------------------------|-------| | **Union Square Greenmarket** | ~600 k | Weekly farmers market; high local foot‑traffic but less overall volume. | | **Brooklyn Flea** | ~400 k | Popular flea market; seasonal and location‑specific. | | **Chelsea Market** | ~1 M | Consistently the highest overall visitor count among indoor markets. | ### Bottom line If you’re looking for the single most‑visited market in New York City, Chelsea Market is the clear leader, drawing a mix of food lovers, shoppers, and tourists every day of the year.
